questions.question: Your teacher writes two number sentences on the whiteboard, one under the other. The top one says 8 + 7 = 15. The bottom one says 800 + 700 = ?. Using the top fact and annexing the zeros, what belongs in the blank?
questions.explain: Add the front digits with a fact to 20 (8 + 7 = 15), then annex the same two zeros that were on each number: 1 500. A common trap is annexing only one zero and writing 150.

questions.question: On a cue card is written the fact 13 - 6 = 7. Right below it is written 13 000 - 6 000 = ?. Using mental math with the fact on the card, what is the answer?
questions.explain: Subtract the front digits (13 - 6 = 7) and annex the three zeros both numbers share, giving 7 000. Watch out for losing a zero and writing 700.

questions.question: A math journal page shows the question 60 000 + 50 000 = ?. Beside it the student has already written the helper fact 6 + 5 = 11. Which line finishes the work correctly?
questions.explain: Each number has four zeros after its front digit, so annex four zeros to 11 and get 110 000. The trap is annexing a different number of zeros than the numbers actually have.

questions.question: A poster in the classroom shows the fact 15 - 7 = 8. Underneath, the teacher has written 1 500 - 700 = ?. What is the missing number?
questions.explain: Use 15 - 7 = 8 and annex the two zeros that both numbers share: 800. Answering 900 usually means the basic fact was recalled wrong (15 - 6 instead of 15 - 7).

questions.question: A water reservoir near Kelowna held 90 000 L of water. After a rainstorm, another 40 000 L flowed in. Using a fact to 20 and annexing the zeros, how much water is in the reservoir now?
questions.explain: Think 9 + 4 = 13, then annex the four zeros that both numbers have: 130 000 L. Dropping a zero and writing 13 000 is the usual slip.

questions.question: A Nanaimo school collected 14 000 bottles in a year-long bottle drive. In January alone they collected 6 000 of them. How many bottles were collected in the rest of the year?
questions.explain: Use the fact 14 - 6 = 8, then annex the three zeros: 8 000 bottles. Answering 7 000 means the basic fact slipped to 13 - 6.

questions.question: Devon wants to find 700 + 500 using mental math instead of paper. Which line shows the strategy used correctly?
questions.explain: Add the front digits with a fact to 20, then annex the two zeros each number carries: 1 200. The trap is annexing the wrong number of zeros, which gives 120 or 12 000.

questions.question: A food bank in Prince George needs 1 600 cans to fill its shelves. So far 900 cans have been donated. How many more cans are needed?
questions.explain: Use the fact 16 - 9 = 7, then annex the two zeros both numbers share: 700 cans. Answering 600 means the fact was recalled as 15 - 9.

questions.question: Jordan is doing mental math and says: 8 + 7 = 15, so 800 + 70 = 1 500. Which statement is correct?
options: Jordan is wrong: the 8 is worth 8 hundreds and the 7 is worth 7 tens, so 800 + 70 = 870.
Jordan should annex just one zero, so 800 + 70 = 150.
Jordan is right, because 8 + 7 = 15 and you annex two zeros.
Jordan should annex three zeros, so 800 + 70 = 15 000.
questions.explain: The annex-the-zeros shortcut only works when both digits sit in the SAME place, so 800 + 70 = 870, not 1 500. Always check the place value of each digit before adding the front digits.

questions.question: The Chan family is driving 2 000 km from Vancouver to visit relatives. On Saturday they drive 900 km and on Sunday they drive 700 km. How many kilometres of the trip are left after Sunday?
questions.explain: First 9 + 7 = 16 gives 1 600 km driven, then 20 - 16 = 4 gives 400 km left. Stopping at 1 600 answers the wrong question, since that is the distance already driven.

questions.question: A ski hill on Mount Seymour sold 900 lift tickets on Saturday and 800 on Sunday. Of all those tickets, 600 were child tickets. How many were adult tickets?
questions.explain: Add first: 9 + 8 = 17, so 1 700 tickets in all; then 17 - 6 = 11, so 1 100 adult tickets. Answering 1 700 means the child tickets were never taken away.

questions.question: A Surrey school raised $6 000 in September and $7 000 in October toward $20 000 of new playground equipment. Ari says: 6 + 7 = 13, so we have $1 300, and we still need $18 700. Which statement is correct?
options: Ari is right; the school still needs $18 700.
The school still needs $70 000, because 20 - 13 = 7 and you annex four zeros.
The school still needs $700, because 20 - 13 = 7 and you annex two zeros.
Ari annexed too few zeros: the school has $13 000, so it still needs $7 000.
questions.explain: Each amount has three zeros, so 6 + 7 = 13 becomes $13 000, and then 20 - 13 = 7 becomes $7 000 still needed. The common trap is annexing fewer zeros than the numbers actually have, which shrinks the money by a whole place value.
